digha_facts_and_secrets.title: Warren Hastings Called It 'The Brighton of the East'
digha_facts_and_secrets.body: In 1780, the first Governor-General of British India, Warren Hastings, was enchanted by Digha's vast flat beaches and wrote a famous letter to his wife praising its calm beauty. His beach retreat was historically called 'Beercool'.

digha_facts_and_secrets.title: Why New Digha Beach Is So Flat & Safe
digha_facts_and_secrets.body: Unlike Puri or Vizag where the continental shelf drops sharply creating violent dumping waves, New Digha's continental slope is among the shallowest in the world. You can safely walk out hundreds of meters during low tide without reaching deep water.

digha_facts_and_secrets.title: The Mohona Sunrise Auction Ritual
digha_facts_and_secrets.body: Between 5:30 AM and 8:30 AM every day, over 400 deep-sea trawlers anchor at Digha Mohona estuary. Hundreds of crates of freshly caught fish are auctioned within seconds in a high-speed rhyming chant by traditional auctioneers (Adatdars).

digha_facts_and_secrets.title: Udaipur Beach: Two States on One Shoreline
digha_facts_and_secrets.body: Just 3 kilometers from New Digha lies Udaipur Beach. The western edge is in Odisha (Baleswar district) while the eastern edge is in West Bengal (Purba Medinipur). You can literally stand with one foot in Bengal and the other in Odisha!

digha_facts_and_secrets.title: Asia's Largest Marine Research Aquarium
digha_facts_and_secrets.body: The Marine Aquarium and Regional Centre (MARC) at Digha, maintained by the Zoological Survey of India, possesses one of the largest closed-circulation marine aquarium display systems in Asia, showcasing over 50 marine species.

digha_facts_and_secrets.title: The Famous Ramnagar Cashew (Kaju) Hub
digha_facts_and_secrets.body: Most tourists don't know that Ramnagar (just 8 km before Digha) is one of Eastern India's primary cashew processing hubs. The coastal soil and salty sea air provide ideal conditions for local cashew plantations.

fish_cooking_benchmarks.disclaimer: Standardized benchmark rates across Digha beach shacks and hotel kitchens. Never pay more than ₹90/kg for plain curry or ₹50/kg for frying.

fry.title: Crispy Deep Fry with Chilies & Onions
fry.description: Oil, turmeric, salt, deep fry with fresh green chilies and onions. Standard: ₹40 - ₹50 / kg.

shorshe.title: Shorshe Ilish / Mustard Paste Gravy
shorshe.description: Ground yellow mustard paste, green chilies, kalonji, mustard oil. Standard: ₹70 - ₹90 / kg.

malaikari.title: Chingri Malaikari (Coconut Cream Curry)
malaikari.description: Rich coconut milk, whole garam masala, ghee gravy. Standard: ₹80 - ₹100 / kg.

kankra_jhal.title: Spicy Coastal Crab Masala (Kankra Jhal)
kankra_jhal.description: Cracking crab shells, rich ginger-garlic and onion-tomato paste. Standard: ₹70 - ₹90 / kg.

patla_jhol.title: Bengali Patla Macher Jhol (Potatoes & Cumin)
patla_jhol.description: Light, digestive cumin and ginger broth with long potato wedges. Standard: ₹50 - ₹70 / kg.
